source.title: STGN: an Implicit Regularization Method for Learning with Noisy Labels in Natural Language Processing
source.authors: Tingting Wu; Xiao Ding; Min-Ji Tang; Haotian Zhang; Bing Qin; Ting Liu

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests a tailored gradient-noise method on noisy-label NLP tasks and reports held-out performance, extending the generalization question to this setting.
record.gate_note: The paper's introductory discussion of memorizing noisy labels cites Zhang et al. (2017); that cited result is not this study's result. The paper does not test the listed claim versions. Its STGN results concern performance under noisy-label training and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study uses noisy-label memorization as motivation for STGN and evaluates its own noise-mitigation method. It does not test V1–V8. Partially corrupted-label training is not V1's comparison of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization; Adam versus Adam plus STGN is not V4's adaptive-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that applying different noise intensities to correct and incorrect samples mitigates label noise across three NLP tasks with synthetic or real-world noise, without requiring a task-specific framework or extensive clean annotations.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces sample-tailored gradient noise during training for noisy-label NLP; the listed versions concern other interventions and measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Label-noise level changes reported SST-5 performance; NoisyNER label sets and wikiHow subtasks also yield different results. The paper reports that removing either guideline can degrade SST-5 performance.

fits_no_version.finding: STGN has higher reported test accuracy or F1 than the corresponding Adam or AdamW baseline across the recorded noisy-label NLP conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-tailored gradient noise can improve held-out performance when NLP models train on noisy labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Figures 1–2 and Section 4.4 report that STGN learns more correct training labels and memorizes fewer incorrect labels than SLN on partially corrupted SST-5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-tailored gradient noise can reduce fitting of corrupted labels while preserving learning of correctly labeled examples.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The paper's limitations state that unmistakably filtering noisy-label data remains challenging. The submitted text does not provide numerical values for Figure 2's memorization and learning ratios.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from the tabulated STGN held-out performance results. The figure-only ratios in Figure 2 are not separately extracted because they do not report explicit numerical values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out generalization under the same architecture and recipe, including chance held-out accuracy for random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimization under limited or broader tuning and the specified recovery conditions.
Batch-size comparisons at fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions across data sizes, dropout strengths, augmentation, and weight-decay conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements, their association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures. Section 3.2's qualitative sharpness argument does not measure these.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples, retraining, and comparison with random removal. STGN perturbs gradients rather than performing this intervention.

record.verdict_notes: Replace the record's tests/T3 classification; its gate_note correctly states that no listed version is tested. The memorization figures do not establish V1's paired capacity-and-generalization result. All recorded numerical comparisons match the supplied tables.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same standard training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the stated architectural comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons under limited and broader tuning, including the listed recovery conditions.
Large versus small batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
